_README.what: Venom & Web: a hand-authored tier of the Permanent Injury Table — one hundred d100 rows for harm done by venom & web, worst at 1 and best at 100.
_README.when: Roll it instead of the Permanent Injury Table when the thing that dropped you was a spider, an ettercap, a snake, a poisoned blade, a sting, a fey toxin or a web — anything that got into the blood or wrapped the body.
_README.contract: Exactly 100 rows, d100 1-100 in order, categories in the shared band order, every injuryType unique within the table AND across every table on the registry (injuryTables.json). `cure` is the LOWEST rung of the shared cure ladder in injuries.json; `duration` is how long it lasts without it. Checked by tools/generate-injury-table.py --check.
_README.status: Hand-authored and locked. Edit rows by hand, keep the count at 100, run the check.

title: Venom & Web
description: What a bite, a sting or a cocoon leaves behind. Low is worse: the bottom is the venom winning, the teens are nerves and lungs that never recover, the middle is weeks of a body clearing poison, the top is a blood that learned something.
rules: A result is a story consequence, not a replacement for a GM ruling. Reroll or override anything that would ruin the table's fun or a player's night.
Roll d100 straight. The Injury Desk's death-save handoff and the Casino's survival roll skip row 1 (Death), because the saves already answered that question.
Low is worse. Rows 1-56 are the price of surviving; 57-70 are a bad week; 71-92 are marks, trauma and oddities; 93-100 are the luck of the survivor.
The cure listed is the LOWEST rung of the shared ladder (injuries.json cureLadder) that removes the row. Anything stronger works too.
Pick the tier table by what did the harm. If nothing on the registry fits, the Permanent Injury Table is the default and always applies.

bands.note: The one row the survival handoff skips.
Alive, and dying on a schedule unless the cure arrives.
The body is not going to be the same.
Weeks, a healer, or second-level magic.
A fortnight of being worse at something.
Shirts off, there is a story.
Months, or a season of care.
Something that should not have happened, did.

cureLadder.note: The ladder is shared: see injuries.json cureLadder. Treatment rows state their Medicine DC inline.

entries.description: You stop. The venom reached the heart before anyone reached you; no saving throw was ever going to argue with it.
entries.notes: Row 1 is skipped by the death-save handoff.

entries.description: The venom is eating what keeps you alive. Your hit point maximum is halved now, and drops by a further 1d6 after every long rest until the cure arrives. At zero you die quietly in your sleep.
entries.duration: Weeks at most without the cure.

entries.description: You were wrapped and hung and the silk's enzyme had started on you before the rescue. Your lungs are burned from the inside: you cannot hold your breath, every Dash costs a level of exhaustion, and a second cocooning kills you outright.

An anticoagulant venom that never left. Any hit that deals piercing or slashing damage keeps bleeding for 1d4 damage at the end of each of your turns until someone spends an action and a DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) check to bind it.
The bitten arm turned black to the shoulder within the hour and was taken off to save the rest of you. You have one arm, and it is the one you did not fight with.
Necrosis took the off arm above the elbow. No shield, no two-handed weapons, no climbing without a check.
The hand that was bitten could not be saved. You can wield one thing at a time and nothing that needs two hands.
The leg below the knee went dark and then went altogether. Speed 20 feet on a crutch or peg; prone whenever you are knocked and cannot stand without a hand.
The bitten foot was amputated at the ankle. Speed reduced by 10 feet; disadvantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks and on saves against being knocked prone.
Lose 1d3 fingers from the bitten hand. With two or more gone you cannot use that hand for fine work, somatic components or a bowstring.

Silk fibres went down with every breath you fought for in the cocoon. Your speed is reduced by 10 feet, you cannot take the Dash action twice in one minute, and smoke or dust forces a Constitution save (DC 12) or you are incapacitated by coughing for a round.

The neurotoxin let one side of your face go. You have disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) and (Performance) checks, and spells with a verbal component fail on a natural 1 on the attack roll or the target's save.
Spat venom took your sight. You are blinded. The eyes are still there, which is why Heal and not Regenerate.

The venom burned the nerves in both hands. Disadvantage on attack rolls with finesse weapons, on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks and on checks with thieves' tools; somatic components are lost on a natural 1.

A relapsing fever the bite left behind. Each dawn roll a d6: on a 1 you have one level of exhaustion that no rest removes until the next dawn. Lesser Restoration ends an episode; only the higher cure ends the disease.
The airway never fully opened again. You speak only in a whisper, cannot shout or sing, and must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save to cast a spell with a verbal component.
One arm and one leg answer slowly. Your speed is halved, you have disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks, and you cannot use a shield.
The ettercap's claw opened a wound that will not close. Your hit point maximum is reduced by 10 until it is cut back to clean tissue (Treatment, DC 15) and allowed a month.
entries.duration: One month after the treatment; permanent without it.

entries.description: A tremor that never stops. Ranged attack rolls beyond 30 feet are made at disadvantage, and you cannot take the Ready action with a ranged weapon.
The venom leached the bones. You take double damage from falls, and any bludgeoning critical hit against you breaks a limb of the GM's choice, splinted and useless for four weeks.
A wound sealed over a plug of web. It festers in cycles: disadvantage on Constitution saving throws, and whenever you take poison damage you gain a level of exhaustion.
entries.duration: Two weeks after it is opened and cleaned (DC 15); permanent without.

entries.description: The heart took the worst of it. Whenever you would gain one level of exhaustion you gain two, and exhaustion level 5 kills you rather than reducing your speed to 0.
The venom reached the inner ear. You are deafened.
Venom in one eye. You are blinded in it: disadvantage on ranged attacks beyond 30 feet and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
A mandible went clean through the hand. You cannot hold a shield or use a two-handed weapon until it heals.
entries.duration: Three weeks after treatment (DC 13); six without.

entries.description: Silk enzyme glued the eyes. You are blinded until the lids are cleaned (Treatment, DC 12, one hour), and have disadvantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks for two weeks after.
Muscle cramps in waves. Your speed is reduced by 10 feet and you have disadvantage on Strength (Athletics) checks.
The calf is swollen hard. Your speed is reduced by 5 feet and you cannot take the Dash action.
entries.duration: Two weeks after treatment (DC 12); four without.

entries.description: A fang went through the cheek. Spells with a verbal component fail on a natural 1 on any d20 you roll for them, and you have disadvantage on Charisma (Performance) checks.
Hallucinations whenever you sleep. A long rest restores only half your Hit Dice, and you cannot benefit from Trance or similar.
A bitten elbow or knee swollen stiff and bound. Your Armour Class is reduced by 2 while it is bound.
Hives across the whole body. Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws and on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, because you scratch.
The anticoagulant is still in you. Each time you take piercing or slashing damage you take a further 1 damage at the end of each of your turns until you receive any healing.
A bitten foot you cannot put weight on. You cannot move more than 20 feet on your turn.
entries.duration: Two weeks after treatment (DC 12); four without.

entries.description: Venom in the forearm. You have disadvantage on checks to grapple or to escape a grapple, and on attack rolls with heavy weapons.
The mind is slow. Disadvantage on Intelligence and Wisdom checks, and you cannot change your prepared spells.
The venom left the nerves raw. Disadvantage on saving throws against being frightened and on Constitution saves to maintain concentration.
Venom burst the vessels in both eyes. Beyond 60 feet everything is a smear: ranged attacks beyond 30 feet are at disadvantage.
You slur. Disadvantage on Charisma (Deception) and (Persuasion) checks.
One level of exhaustion that no rest removes until the fever breaks.
The bitten hand buzzes. Disadvantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks and on checks with thieves' tools.
Two fang holes that will not stay closed. Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws against disease.
entries.duration: Two weeks after treatment (DC 10); a month without.

entries.description: The venom primed you for the next one. Any poison damage you take is increased by 1d4.
Silk friction burn the length of the forearm. Disadvantage on ability checks that use that arm.
You wrenched your back fighting the silk. Wearing heavy armour for a day costs a level of exhaustion.
Bright light splits the head. You have disadvantage on attack rolls while in bright light.
One eye swollen shut. Disadvantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks and on ranged attack rolls.
The ettercap's grip bruised everything under the ribs. Your hit point maximum is reduced by 5.
Stiff from hanging in the web. Disadvantage on initiative rolls.
Your body does not clear it. Any poisoned condition you suffer lasts twice as long.
The drawing wrist. Ranged weapon attack rolls are made at disadvantage.
entries.duration: Two weeks after treatment (DC 12); four without.

entries.description: The venom washed the colour out. You cannot distinguish colours, and have disadvantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks that depend on sight.
A fine shake in the legs. Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
Silk in the chest. You cannot hold your breath, and you have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks because of the coughing.
entries.duration: Two weeks after treatment (DC 12); four without.

entries.description: A bite under the foot. Your speed is reduced by 5 feet.
The body remembers the first bite. You have disadvantage on your first attack roll in each combat.
A clean bite that needs cleaning daily: a DC 8 Wisdom (Medicine) check each morning, or it becomes Weeping Punctures (42).
Silk residue in your hair and clothes. Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks until you get an hour, hot water and soap.
The bite itches without pause. Disadvantage on Constitution saves to maintain concentration.
Bitten on the mouth. Disadvantage on Charisma (Performance) checks.
A toe you cannot feel. Disadvantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.
Spider hairs in the skin of the hands. Disadvantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks.
A plug of silk in one ear. Disadvantage on hearing-based Wisdom (Perception) checks until it is flushed (Treatment, DC 8).
entries.duration: Ten minutes with a healer; a week without.

entries.description: A fang caught the thumb. Disadvantage on checks with thieves' tools.
Nothing stays down. Any potion you drink in the next day has a 50 percent chance to come back up with no effect.
The web took the skin off your palm. Climbing costs you triple movement instead of double.
A nick on the neck that will scar small. You take 1 extra damage from the next poison effect that hits you.
The last of the venom. Disadvantage on initiative rolls.
A welt across the eyes where the strand hit. Disadvantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.
Nothing lasting. You check every boot before you put it on for the rest of your life.
Two puckered holes under the cheekbone. Advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks against anyone who has seen an ettercap; disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks with children.
The lips stayed dark. Strangers assume poisoner: disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks with merchants and guards who do not know you.
The eye clouded white but sees. Advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks; disadvantage on Charisma (Deception) checks, because everyone looks at the eye.
A thin white line where a strand cut across the face. Cosmetic. People trace it with their eyes while you talk.
One cheek never went down. Disadvantage on Charisma (Performance) checks.
Two deep dimples that show through a thin shirt. Cosmetic.
A patch of skin across the back bleached white in the pattern of the web. Cosmetic, and unmistakable.
A black-edged scar where the rot was cut out before it spread. Healers recognise the work; so do people who have buried someone it was not cut out of.
You are frightened of any spider larger than a hand while it is within 30 feet of you, unless you succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw at the start of your turn.
entries.duration: Months — or a season of care.

entries.description: The cocoon stays with you. You cannot enter a space narrower than 5 feet without a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until you leave it.
entries.duration: Months — or a season of care.

entries.description: You feel webs on your skin that are not there. Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks: you keep brushing them off.
entries.duration: Months — or a season of care.

entries.description: You check every corner before you enter. Disadvantage on initiative rolls in enclosed spaces.
entries.duration: Months — or a season of care.

entries.description: Forests are not restful. A long rest taken under trees restores only half your Hit Dice.
entries.duration: Months — or a season of care.

entries.description: Disadvantage on saving throws against being frightened by a beast or monstrosity.
entries.duration: Months — or a season of care.

entries.description: You sleep badly. On each long rest roll a d6: on a 1 you gain no benefit from it.
entries.duration: Months — or a season of care.

entries.description: Being grappled is being wrapped. While grappled you are also frightened of the creature grappling you.
entries.duration: Months — or a season of care.

entries.description: The hair on your arms rises when there is a web within 30 feet. No rule attaches; the GM may give you a hint a round early.
entries.duration: Permanent — if you wanted it gone.

entries.description: The bite healed in a ring of pale dots that grove-folk and ettercap hunters recognise on sight. They treat you as one of theirs, which is not always a compliment.
Once per long rest you can coat a blade in your own blood: the next hit deals an extra 1d4 poison damage. You have disadvantage on saving throws against poison.
Your sweat is faintly adhesive. Advantage on ability checks made to climb; disadvantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks.
You dream what the nearest spider sees. Once a week the GM gives you one true image of a spider-haunted place.
You understand, but cannot speak, the clicking of ettercaps. They notice you noticing.
The bite that nearly killed you taught your blood something. Advantage on saving throws against poison from beasts and monstrosities.
The bite healed clean and fast. The next time you are poisoned, the condition ends at the start of your next turn.
Advantage on checks made to escape being restrained by webs, nets or similar.
Spiders of animal intelligence do not attack you first if another target is available.
You can always tell by touch whether a web was spun within the last hour.
Resistance to poison damage.
Once, when poison damage would reduce you to 0 hit points, you drop to 1 instead and shed every poison effect on you. Then the row is spent.
You stand up at 1 hit point, and the creature that dropped you takes poison damage equal to your hit point maximum as its own venom turns in its glands.
